_about: Shot plan for baseline_shoot.py: the neutral (no Look Grade, no LUT) reference set the Looks Lab is built from. Edit freely; run 'python baseline_shoot.py TAG --dry-run' to see the resulting matrix and count before queueing it.

times._note: One row per shot time, for the SUN-DRIVEN period model below (fork branch foxnne/scene-periods-sun, periodsFollowSun on). 'hour' is what you edit; the real Scene Manager period weights are computed from 'period_model' and written to the manifest. Each hour sits where its period has full weight AND the scene shows that period's light: the sun here rises 07:30 and sets 18:30 (alternate path, 55 deg at 13:00), climbs about 13 deg per hour near the horizon by day and 11 deg per hour below it. Pure periods with the defaults: Dawn 07:12-07:22, Sunrise 07:37-08:08, Day 08:22-17:38, Sunset 17:52-18:23, Dusk 18:38-18:48, Night 19:05-06:56. The table used before is kept as 'times_clock' (python baseline_shoot.py TAG --period-model clock).

Dawn.note: 07:20, sun -1.9 deg rising: brightest part of pure Dawn (100% Dawn), first usable twilight before the direct light arrives

Sunrise.note: 07:51, sun +4.7 deg rising: middle of pure Sunrise (100%), richest warm low sun

Day.note: solar noon, sun 55 deg: pure Day

Sunset.note: 18:09, sun +4.7 deg setting: middle of pure Sunset (100%), inside the observed colour peak 18:00-18:25

Dusk.note: 18:40, sun -1.9 deg setting: brightest part of pure Dusk (100%), last usable twilight (dark by about 18:50)

times_clock._note: The previous table, for the CLOCK period model ('period_model_clock'; the fork with periodsFollowSun off, and every build before foxnne/scene-periods-sun). Used with --period-model clock. In this setup 07:00 is still dark, sunset colour peaks about 18:00-18:25 and it is dark by 18:50, so pure clock Dawn and Dusk are dark and these hours sit inside blends.

Dawn.note: first light; Scene Manager: about 90% Dawn, 10% Sunrise (pure Dawn 06:00-07:00 is still dark here)

Sunset.note: peak sunset colour; about 99% Sunset (pure Sunset 17:00-18:00, then blends to Dusk until 19:00)

Dusk.note: after-glow, nearly dark; about 84% Dusk, 16% Sunset (pure Dusk 19:00-20:00 is already night-dark here)

period_model._note: kind 'sun': the fork's sun-driven periods (src/CSEditor/SceneManager/ScenePeriodSun.h, SceneSettingsManager::GetSunPeriodFactors). The weights come from the sun's elevation on Sky Sync's path: Night below night_elevation, Dawn / Dusk up to horizon_elevation, Sunrise / Sunset up to day_elevation, Day above, each boundary blended over blend_degrees (full width, centred). 'sun' describes that path: 'alternate' = Sky Sync's alternate sun path (pack foxnne-look sets UseAlternateSunPath), tilt 55 = SunPath Southern; 'timing' = the climate's TNAM sunrise begin/end, sunset begin/end in 10-minute units (SkyrimClimate, winner NAT-ENB.esp, vanilla values). The elevations / blend must equal the Scene Manager's 'Day Above', 'Night Below' and 'Sun Period Blend' sliders (defaults 10, -5, 3). The clock fields below are unused while kind is 'sun'. Not read from the running game: check the Scene Manager debug section once.

period_model_clock._note: The model before periods followed the sun: how the fork's Scene Manager turns the game hour into period weights from the climate's clock timing (SceneSettingsManager.cpp: GetPeriodStartHours, GetBlendedPeriods, FindBlendPeriod, GetTimeOfDayFactors). 'starts' come from the active climate: SkyrimClimate as overridden by NAT-ENB.esp keeps the vanilla timing (sunrise 5:30-10:00, sunset 16:00-20:30) and fDaytimeColorExtension is assumed vanilla (0.5). Still what the game does with 'Periods Follow the Sun' off or where Sky Sync places no sun.

sky._note: mode 'types_json': apply each sky type's Physical Sky / fog / ambient values from the pass-3 types file on top of the saved settings (Day values plus the override of the dominant period), like sky_sweep.py --stock with sweeps/pass3_types_*.json. mode 'scene': set only weather and hour and let an installed pack drive the sky (use this once the cloud pack is installed).

interior_matrix._note: Interior and dungeon views do not follow the outdoor matrix: they are shot once per listed time. Since 2026-11-20 the script sets no weather for them (and releases a weather lock before going indoors): the cell keeps its own interior weather.

neutral._note: What makes a shot neutral for the lab: the two stages after tone mapping that the lab replaces are OFF. The script sets and reads these back before every shot and aborts on a mismatch.
